title: Automatic Argument Quality Assessment: New Datasets and Methods
task_or_target: expert-calibrated argument quality ranking and pair classification
comparison_or_outcome_labels: 14k independently annotated argument pairs with higher-quality member identified; separate 6.3k pointwise arguments
domain_language: online debates and web arguments; English
limitations_or_gap: Quality is not explicit defeat or proof validity; crowd judgments rather than domain-expert adjudication; no tie/incomparability class
evidence_note: Official ACL paper reports pairwise quality labels and ranking evaluation with annotator quality controls

title: Efficient Pairwise Annotation of Argument Quality
task_or_target: multi-dimensional argument quality ranking from sparse pairwise judgments
comparison_or_outcome_labels: 41,859 pairwise judgments aggregated into rhetorical logical dialectical and overall scores
limitations_or_gap: Closest public benchmark to multi-dimensional strength but labels are inferred quality scores rather than explicit attack defeat burden or incomparability
evidence_note: Official ACL abstract gives corpus size dimensions and pairwise aggregation procedure

title: Ranking Passages for Argument Convincingness
authors: Peter Potash; Adam Ferguson; Timothy J. Hazen
task_or_target: pairwise ranking of passages supporting opposing stances
comparison_or_outcome_labels: pairwise winner labels with transitivity filtering and win-rate/PageRank aggregation
argument_representation: text passages aligned to topic stance
scale_or_size: pairwise-labeled passage corpus; exact total not stated in abstract
limitations_or_gap: Persuasiveness may diverge from logical support; crowd labels and no structured argument graph or explicit abstention
evidence_note: Official ACL abstract states pairwise annotation task and transitivity filtering

title: Are You Convinced? Choosing the More Convincing Evidence with a Siamese Network
task_or_target: pairwise evidence convincingness
comparison_or_outcome_labels: each evidence pair labeled for which is more convincing
limitations_or_gap: Narrow convincingness target; no expert philosophical/legal rubric, defeat relation, burden, or incomparability
evidence_note: Official ACL page describes IBM-EviConv as a new challenging pairwise convincingness dataset

title: Finding Convincing Arguments Using Scalable Bayesian Preference Learning
task_or_target: preference learning and ranking of convincing arguments
comparison_or_outcome_labels: crowdsourced pairwise preferences with inferred rankings
scale_or_size: UKP convincingness corpus family; count varies by release
limitations_or_gap: Method paper and corpus are preference-based but not expert adjudication; convincingness is audience-relative and lacks formal defeat labels
evidence_note: Official TACL abstract describes predicting convincingness from crowdsourced preference data and rankings

title: A Large-scale Dataset for Argument Quality Ranking: Construction and Analysis
task_or_target: large-scale argument quality ranking
comparison_or_outcome_labels: quality scores and pairwise/ranking use over debate arguments
limitations_or_gap: Large-scale ranking is useful for calibration but aggregate quality is not proof strength, defeat, dominance, or incomparability
evidence_note: ArXiv abstract identifies the dataset and argument quality ranking task

title: ArgAnalysis35K: A large-scale dataset for Argument Quality Analysis
authors: Omkar Joshi; Priya Pitre; Yashodhara Haribhakta
task_or_target: argument-analysis pair classification and relevance/quality assessment
comparison_or_outcome_labels: 34,890 high-quality argument-analysis pairs with reliability-aware labels
limitations_or_gap: Authors have parliamentary-debate experience but labels are not expert legal/philosophical adjudication and do not encode defeat or abstention
evidence_note: Official ACL abstract reports combined 10+ years of parliamentary debating experience and 34,890 pairs

title: Persuasiveness of Generated Free-Text Rationales in Subjective Decisions: A Case Study on Pairwise Argument Ranking
task_or_target: pairwise argument preference plus rationale persuasiveness evaluation
comparison_or_outcome_labels: winner/preference labels and pairwise rationale judgments
scale_or_size: IBM-9k and IBM-30k-derived pairwise rationale comparisons
limitations_or_gap: Useful for judging explanations alongside preference but not formal strength semantics or expert domain calibration
evidence_note: ACL paper reports pairwise ranking of rationales and human evaluation procedures

title: Learning From Revisions: Quality Assessment of Claims in Argumentation at Scale
authors: Gabriella Skitalinskaya; Jonas Klaff; Henning Wachsmuth
task_or_target: better-claim pair classification and ranking across revisions
comparison_or_outcome_labels: 377k-plus claim revision pairs with pairwise better-claim labels and version rankings
argument_representation: claims and revisions in structured online argumentation
domain_language: politics ethics entertainment and other Kialo topics; English
limitations_or_gap: Scale is excellent but revision quality is not argument defeat or reason strength; no domain-expert rubric or incomparable outcome
evidence_note: ACL abstract and official repository describe pairwise ranking task and released data/scripts

title: ArgBench: Benchmarking LLMs on Computational Argumentation Tasks
task_or_target: multi-task argument mining quality assessment reasoning and generation
comparison_or_outcome_labels: 46 tasks across 33 datasets with task-specific labels and metrics
argument_representation: mixed argumentative text relations and reasoning items
scale_or_size: 46 tasks from 33 datasets with train/validation/test splits
limitations_or_gap: Broad coverage but heterogeneous tasks do not isolate expert pairwise strength or explicit defeat/dominance/incomparability
evidence_note: Official ACL abstract and data repository describe 46 tasks and five skill groups

title: This House Debates AI: Evaluating a Language Model in Oxford-Style Debates against Human Experts
task_or_target: multi-turn competing-argument evaluation against experienced human debaters
comparison_or_outcome_labels: 5 independent raters provide win/loss judgments and 0-100 scores across 11 quality dimensions
scale_or_size: 100 debates; 20 experienced human debaters; 5 raters per debate
limitations_or_gap: Strongest recent expert-calibration resource but debate winner is not a proposition-level defeat graph and artifact release/access must be checked
evidence_note: Official ACL abstract reports 100 debates 20 experienced debaters five raters and win/loss plus 11 dimensions

title: Argument Quality Assessment with Large Language Models: A Pairwise Bradley-Terry Approach
authors: Nicolás Benjamín Ocampo; Agnes Paullate Nyiranziza; Davide Ceolin
task_or_target: LLM pairwise comparisons calibrated against expert argument-quality judgments
comparison_or_outcome_labels: logical rhetorical and dialectical pairwise labels with Bradley-Terry latent strength scores
scale_or_size: 12 open-weight LLMs and expert comparison trials
limitations_or_gap: Evaluation paper rather than a clearly released benchmark artifact; expert pool/task construction and access require verification; quality dimensions remain non-formal
evidence_note: ArXiv abstract explicitly states approximation of expert pairwise comparisons and Bradley-Terry ranking

title: PRBench: Large-Scale Expert Rubrics for Evaluating High-Stakes Professional Reasoning
task_or_target: expert-calibrated legal and finance reasoning
comparison_or_outcome_labels: 19,356 expert-curated criteria over 1,100 expert-authored tasks with independent expert validation
domain_language: law and finance across 114 countries and 47 US jurisdictions
limitations_or_gap: Not pairwise argument comparison; strongest as a legal expert-rubric calibration layer for reasoning quality and process completeness
evidence_note: Official ACL abstract reports expert authorship qualifications rubric validation and legal coverage

title: PLAWBENCH: A Rubric-Based Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs in Real-World Legal Practice
task_or_target: expert-rubric legal reasoning and document generation
comparison_or_outcome_labels: approximately 12,500 rubric items attached to 850 questions across 13 legal scenarios
argument_representation: legal consultation case analysis and document generation
domain_language: real-world legal practice; English/Chinese source materials
limitations_or_gap: Not pairwise argument ranking; useful for calibrating substantive legal reasoning and rubric agreement rather than winner labels
evidence_note: Official ACL abstract states expert-designed rubrics and evaluator alignment with human experts

title: LAR-ECHR: A New Legal Argument Reasoning Task and Dataset for Cases of the European Court of Human Rights
task_or_target: select next statement in a chain of legal arguments
comparison_or_outcome_labels: correct next-statement labels from court-proceeding argument chains
argument_representation: structured legal argument chains from ECHR cases
scale_or_size: case-based legal argument dataset; exact total not stated in ACL abstract
limitations_or_gap: Expert/legal reasoning calibration but not pairwise comparison; multiple-choice next-step labels omit relative strength and incomparable outcomes
evidence_note: Official ACL abstract defines the legal-argument-chain task and cross-benchmark model-ranking comparison

title: Audiences and Argument Strength
task_or_target: formal ranking of competing arguments under audiences and values
comparison_or_outcome_labels: ranking-based semantics compare individual arguments and audience/value settings change relative strength
limitations_or_gap: Direct strength-ranking control but lacks natural-language arguments human/expert labels and explicit incomparability
evidence_note: Official competition paper describes ranking-based semantics and comparison of individual arguments

title: Towards Ranking Arguments in Incomplete Argumentation Frameworks
task_or_target: ranking under uncertain or incomplete attacks
comparison_or_outcome_labels: ranking semantics over incomplete frameworks with structural uncertainty
limitations_or_gap: Useful formal control for uncertainty but not expert pairwise judgments or authentic philosophical/legal arguments
evidence_note: Official competition paper frames ranking semantics for incomplete frameworks

title: The Fourth International Competition on Computational Models of Argumentation
task_or_target: formal acceptance and reasoning under argumentation semantics
comparison_or_outcome_labels: credulous/sceptical acceptance extension enumeration and solver correctness tasks
limitations_or_gap: Defeat semantics are explicit but tasks force acceptance decisions rather than graded expert strength or incomparability
evidence_note: Official ICCMA benchmark and solver documents define benchmark selection and acceptance tasks

title: Argument Quality Assessment with Expert Pairwise Comparisons in Legal and Philosophical Reasoning
task_or_target: calibration set for proposition-level pairwise strength judgments
comparison_or_outcome_labels: expert winner/loser/tie/incomparable plus reason-coded adjudication and confidence
argument_representation: paired reconstructed arguments with cited source spans
domain_language: legal and philosophical texts; multilingual extension possible
limitations_or_gap: No existing source found that combines expert pairwise comparison with explicit defeat burden incomparability and provenance; this row records the uncovered target rather than an existing benchmark
evidence_note: Gap synthesis from direct pairwise corpora and expert legal/debate rubric benchmarks

title: Which Side Are You On? A Multi-task Dataset for End-to-End Argument Summarisation and Evaluation
resource_or_benchmark: argument mining and evaluation multi-task dataset
task_or_target: evidence convincingness ranking and human preference ranking for debate essays
comparison_or_outcome_labels: evidence convincingness ranking human preference ranking and quality dimensions
limitations_or_gap: Combines preference and convincingness but does not make defeat burden dominance or incomparability first-class labels
evidence_note: ACL abstract enumerates evidence detection convincingness ranking human preference ranking and quality evaluation tasks

title: Evaluating Legal Reasoning Traces with Legal Issue Tree Rubrics
task_or_target: expert-level legal reasoning trace evaluation over opposing-party arguments and court conclusions
comparison_or_outcome_labels: 24K instances with hierarchical issue-tree rubrics; human-expert reliability validation for issue coverage and correctness
argument_representation: court judgments converted to hierarchical trees of opposing arguments and conclusions
limitations_or_gap: Not pairwise winner/loser annotation; strongest for expert-calibrated coverage/correctness of legal reasoning traces and structured opposition
evidence_note: ACL abstract reports 24K instances, opposing-party argument trees, court conclusions, and human expert rubric validation

title: GreekBarBench: A Challenging Benchmark for Free-Text Legal Reasoning and Citations
task_or_target: free-text legal reasoning, citation, and LLM-judge meta-evaluation against human experts
comparison_or_outcome_labels: expert-evaluation correlation benchmark; span-based rubrics improve LLM-judge alignment with human expert evaluations
argument_representation: free-text legal answers with citations and span-level rubric evidence
domain_language: Greek legal reasoning; Greek/English evaluation materials
scale_or_size: benchmark scale not stated in search abstract
limitations_or_gap: Not a direct pairwise argument-ranking corpus; useful for expert calibration, citation grounding, and judge agreement in legal reasoning
evidence_note: ACL abstract explicitly describes a meta-evaluation benchmark for LLM-judge versus human-expert correlation and span-based rubrics
